objective: Build the arm64 image the robot actually needs on a native arm64 runner, name the architecture in the image tag so a pull cannot silently fetch amd64, smoke-test it with the existing script, and state in the deployment doc which architectures are published.
decision_supported: Does an arm64 image exist for the Jetson, and can a deployment pull an amd64 image by mistake?
acceptance: A documented arm64 build path exists and runs on a native arm64 runner, with the choice and its cost recorded because a qemu cross-build of a CUDA base is slow.
The image tag names the architecture for both amd64 and arm64, so a latest pull on the robot cannot silently fetch an amd64 image.
The arm64 job asserts the built image really is aarch64, because a mislabelled image would pass every other step.
A smoke test runs the offline demo and the dashboard health check in the arm64 image, and reuses the existing check_arm64_environment.sh rather than a second recipe.
docs/deployment/container.md states which architectures are published and which are not.
The integrations README stops pointing at docs/PORTABILITY.md, which never existed, and points at the deployment page instead.
evidence: pytest tests/unit/test_arm64_image.py: 16 passed, covering the native runner, the absent platforms key, the architecture-named tags, the entrypoint arch assertion and the documented architectures.
The workflow YAML parses with four jobs and no paths filter on any trigger.
check_doc_references.py: PASS, 182 pages, so the reference to the deployment page resolves.
make docs, ruff check and ruff format --check clean.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: The arm64 build would have to be run to claim it produces a working image; this container is amd64 with no Docker, so the job is unexecuted here and the pull request says so.
A qemu cross-build would have to be used because no arm64 runner were available; ubuntu-24.04-arm is available, so that fallback is not taken.
The existing arm64 smoke script would have to be replaced by a second recipe; it is reused instead.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to the Dockerfile or to the release workflow.
data_classification: Repository-local workflow configuration, Markdown and Python. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets.
model_policy: Deterministic YAML and pytest; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: The arm64 build is unexecuted here. A first-order risk is that the CUDA base has no arm64 manifest for this tag; that surfaces as a build failure naming the base image, and the Dockerfile is the file to change.

Renaming the amd64 tag could break a consumer that used the old name. Every reference in the workflow was updated in the same change and a test asserts the build and the run steps agree, and the tag was never published, so nothing outside CI pulled it.
A native arm64 runner is slower per core than the amd64 one, so the arm64 job may take longer. It is bounded by timeout-minutes and cached under its own scope, so it cannot evict the amd64 cache.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: the arm64 job disappears and the amd64 tag returns to its architecture-less name. Nothing else reads either.
